quest.title: Divine Plant of the Depths
quest.description: Does ancient plant life from the ocean's depths really have the wondrous power to indicate one's destiny?
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Hero's Wit x3, Mora x30000

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: Hello there, youngster. From how you dress, you must be from outside the island, yes?

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Ah, then you must be some manner of traveler, then? Well... Would you like to stop here for awhile and divine your way forward?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh, divining?

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Hahaha, no, no, there's no need to be so worried. I apologize, it was a bit sudden of me...

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: What I mean to say is, the shrine to Watatsumi here in Bourou Village is most efficacious, which is why I offered you a divination.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: I did not mean to imply that the road ahead would be perilous.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: I mean, how can our paths be encompassed by a mere few words? That is quite preposterous, of course.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so it's just fortune-telling, huh? Well, that's a relief!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How much will it cost?

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Oh, it costs nothing. We do not ask for money over such things...

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: If those who man the shrines were to collect money over such a thing as "wishes," we will surely disturb Omikami's great spirit.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: We are all mortals, after all. How could we dare to profit off the wishes of others?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so that's how it is.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: So then, would you two be interested in a little fortune-telling?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, we'll give it a go.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Haha, you have my thanks.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: In this time, there is little peace to be found anywhere, and the young people of the village are busying themselves elsewhere. Seeing you youngsters come here does warm the cockles of this old heart.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: That you are outlanders who treat the traditions of Watatsumi Island with respect is rarer still. Impressive indeed, haha...

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Alright, I shan't nag. Now, as for the fortune-telling...

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Before we begin, would the two of you mind helping this old lady with something?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, is this about Mora after all?

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Hehe, no, no... Come, just listen to me.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: The efficacy of the shrine here in Bourou Village is derived from the "Deep Sea Spiritherb" grown there.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: As the name might indicate, this plant once grew at the bottom of the ocean... which is where our ancestors came from.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Thousands of years ago, the progenitors of our village transplanted those herbs from the deep sea onto land and raised them very carefully.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Under the care of generation after generation of our village's people, neither wars nor natural disasters, or even the great sorrow of our Omikami's martyrdom, have managed to destroy these long-lived Spiritherbs.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: This plant grows beneath the waters, so it needs a frequent supply of water to survive.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: And it also gives off a gentle, constant light, owing to having lived in utter darkness.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: As such, we use the brilliance of its light to judge if the wishes made can be realized, and the heart of this mystery is the water source.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Hehe, the younger shrine maidens often doubt the trustworthiness of the divining ritual. They feel that it is insufficiently official, or tantamount to spreading superstition... and other things like that.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: They prefer theories that are clearer and easy to understand, and lack fondness for word-of-mouth legends that tend to decay over time.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Still... the wisdom of the ancients, the knowledge that was passed down from one generation to the next...

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: While it may not be easily unified into some clear theory or another, it does still contain certain truths that cannot be ignored.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, you were talking about the water source...

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Water source...? Oh! Hehe, right! Ah, just listen to me prattle on. My age really is catching up with me, isn't it?

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Now then, water from the Offering Pool on this island's shrine is required to raise Spiritherbs. This is because the water there contains "wishes."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Can water really contain something like that?

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Hehe, of course. Everyone's "wishes" will accumulate within that pool and dissolve into the water, just like honey.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: No one can see it, no, but they can tell by the sweetness and viscosity of the water.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: So it is with memory, and so it is with faith... They all follow this principle.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Ah, yes. If you go to draw water, do be careful... The power of these wishes will soon dissipate into the air once you leave the Offering Pool...

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Just like dreams flow away as the years pass...

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: The dissipation of these wishes, too, can be detected by their touch and weight.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Huh...

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Haha, sorry, sorry, I seem to have gone off topic again...

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Either way, return here immediately and do not tarry once you have drawn the water.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Otherwise, the power of those wishes will fully dissipate, and the Spiritherbs will not receive proper nutrition...

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Once this is done, do remind me once again... There is another step required to nourish the Spiritherb and ensure the efficacy of our divination.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is pretty troublesome. Don't you have any shrine maidens to help you out, Granny?

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: *sigh* The young shrine maidens nowadays consider such things bothersome. They turn their noses up at these ancient traditions and generally refuse to help.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: It is simply depressing beyond measure to watch as the Spiritherbs' glow grows dimmer with each passing day...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But y'know, it is kinda troublesome...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I kind of understand the shrine maidens' perspective now...

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Well then. Will you help me draw some water or not?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh, we'll help alright.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: In that case, you have my thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: You're back.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We've brought what you asked for.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Clean water, fresh outta the Offering Pool!

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: Ah, thank you both so much. Come now, allow me to give this water to the Spiritherbs.

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: And yes, where was I... Ah, right. There is another step to make the Spiritherbs more radiant still.

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: The stem and leaves of the Spiritherb will only be truly at home, and thus display the vibrant of color of "wishes," when it is in an environment rich with Hydro from the deep sea.

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: Simply put... There is a cavern to the north where the Hydro composition of the water is closest to the natural environment of this plant.

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: The concentration also differs from place to place within this cavern. Of them, the Hydro concentration you are looking for is something crystal-clear and transparent.

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: But things might get difficult if the water grows turbid, or if you are interrupted by other life forms...

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: *sigh* At my age, I cannot quite be sure of the meaning of these words.

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: Nonetheless, I trust that you will understand it when you see it.

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: That cavern is tightly bound to the secret of our ancestors. Unfortunately, with the recent war, few young people have gone there to draw water and nourish the Spiritherbs.

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: *sigh* Speaking of our young people, I can only hope that they will return safely...

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: Ah yes. If you want to go there to draw water, youngster, please be very careful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Granny, we'll be fine!

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Good, good. Thank you both very much.

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: Ah, you've returned. Come, come, have a rest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Granny Komaki, we've brought the water you asked for!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is the "ideal water" you spoke of, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: Yes, and this amount will do the job as well. Thank you for the trouble...

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: Haha, ah, look at them...

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: From the Spiritherbs' radiance... The year to come will surely be a peaceful and abundant one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, how could you tell?

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: The color of the Spiritherbs has always been dependent on the moisture it gets, and the nourishment it gains from the wishes of the people.

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: This soul-light is the embodiment of those wishes — the better the wishes, the more vibrant the light, and the more hope there is in our future.

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: After all, everyone wishes for a better tomorrow, don't they?

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: As long everyone wishes to do something to improve on their present lives a little...

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: Even something as terrible as a war's aftermath may yet prove to be a small affair in comparison.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... So does this have anything to do with its... efficacy?

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: Of course. This is the wisdom of us old folks, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: Wishes drive and encourage people, and the results of their actions verify their wishes in turn.

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: As long as we are able to protect our peaceful lives, and as long as we can hold on to hope even during dark days...

dialogues.speaker: Komaki
dialogues.text: The divinations of the Spiritherb will always be efficacious.

choices.text: This feels like a perfunctory explanation for a superstition...

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Hehe. Ah, youngster, you will understand someday.

response.speaker: Komaki
response.text: Ah, by the way, the power of the wishes within the water will last a few days more. If you are willing, you can come by again anytime for another divination.

choices.text: But it isn't entirely without merit...

talks.objective: Return to the village in time
Go to the cave that Komaki mentioned
